governanceNotes: D1 batch 68 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - papilledema to visual-impairment (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the 490-patient IIH prospective cohort (worst visual outcomes with the most severe papilledema; PMID 36242625), the IIH Intervention trial protocol (permanent visual loss due to papilloedema; PMID 42547236), and the CVST-versus-IIH graded visual-assessment cohort (PMID 42435089).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) shared-driver limit - raised intracranial pressure causes both the disc edema and (through multiple routes) the visual loss, so the edge's independent-mechanism claim is bounded and carried openly; (ii) intermediate-pathway discipline - the papilledema-to-secondary-optic-atrophy step is recorded on the edge's mechanism narrative but NOT authored as its own edge, to avoid duplicating the batch-66 optic-atrophy to visual-impairment chain (chain-triangle semantics under the standing CRG follow-up); (iii) parallel-manifestation withhold - sixth-nerve palsy (diplopia in the IIH group) is a raised-ICP manifestation shared with papilledema, not a downstream consequence; (iv) etiology scope - IIH dominates the anchors; the CVST comparison shows papilledema grade and visual measures differ by etiology; (v) ME-29 - the hydrocephalus visual-impairment window's papilledema-anchored pediatric data are not recycled here.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Papilledema documents visual acuity and field impairment at prospective-cohort and trial-protocol level: the 9-year idiopathic intracranial hypertension prospective cohort of 490 patients found those with the highest OCT retinal nerve fibre layer (most severe papilledema) had the worst visual outcomes, with delayed visual field and ganglion cell layer decline after 12 months and disease duration a key visual prognostic factor (PMID 36242625), the IIH Intervention randomized trial protocol states patients are at risk of permanent visual loss due to papilledema and uses peripapillary nerve fibre layer and perimetric mean deviation as its vision-preservation endpoints (PMID 42547236), and the CVST-versus-IIH papilledema cohort documents graded visual assessment (Frisen grade, scotomas, nerve fibre layer, perimetric mean deviation) across etiologies (PMID 42435089); recorded as documented association only with the etiology-spanning scope carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the anchors are idiopathic-intracranial-hypertension-dominant raised-pressure populations in which papilledema severity and visual loss both track the underlying pressure burden (shared-driver confounding), so whether any individual visual impairment is attributable to the disc edema itself requires individual neuro-ophthalmologic assessment with glaucomatous, retinal, and refractive exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Sustained optic disc edema with axoplasmic flow stasis and compression of disc microcirculation drives retinal ganglion cell axon injury so visual field and acuity loss result, the compression-ischemia route supported by the severity gradient (highest nerve fibre layer worst visual outcomes) and the vision-preservation trial rationale that reducing papilledema preserves vision, but whether this route produced any individual visual impairment remains hypothesized until perimetry and OCT records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single prospective cohort (490 patients) plus trial-protocol and cross-etiology comparison class only: the cohort is idiopathic-intracranial-hypertension-dominant so etiology generalization is partial, papilledema severity and visual loss co-vary with intracranial pressure so the disc edema's independent contribution is not isolated, and the vision-preservation trial is a protocol without efficacy data.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The anchors are IIH-dominant so papilledema of other etiologies (mass lesions, venous sinus thrombosis, malignant hypertension) is underrepresented; severity of papilledema and severity of visual loss share the intracranial-pressure driver so independent attribution is limited; the IIH Intervention trial contributes protocol framing only; the CVST-IIH comparison shows etiologic differences in papilledema grade and visual measures; and glaucoma, retinal disease, refractive error, and medication effects compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: the underlying raised-intracranial-pressure cause driving both papilledema and visual loss (shared driver; IIH, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, mass lesions)
glaucoma and other optic neuropathies (the published windows, not recycled per ME-29)

evidenceGaps: The anchors are IIH-dominant so papilledema of other etiologies (mass lesions, venous sinus thrombosis, malignant hypertension) is underrepresented; severity of papilledema and severity of visual loss share the intracranial-pressure driver so independent attribution is limited; the IIH Intervention trial contributes protocol framing only; the CVST-IIH comparison shows etiologic differences in papilledema grade and visual measures; and glaucoma, retinal disease, refractive error, and medication effects compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prospective-cohort plus trial-protocol class with the shared-driver and etiology limits carried openly: the 490-patient IIH prospective cohort found worst visual outcomes with the most severe papilledema on OCT with delayed decline (PMID 36242625), the IIH Intervention protocol frames permanent visual loss as due to papilloedema with vision-preservation endpoints (PMID 42547236), and the CVST-versus-IIH cohort documents graded visual assessment across etiologies (PMID 42435089); because papilledema severity and visual loss share the intracranial-pressure driver and the anchors are IIH-dominant, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated neuro-ophthalmologic assessment with perimetry, OCT, and glaucomatous, retinal, and refractive exclusion.

sourceReferences.citation: Thaller M, Homer V, Hyder Y, et al. The idiopathic intracranial hypertension prospective cohort study: evaluation of prognostic factors and outcomes J Neurol. 2023 Feb;270(2):851-863. PMID 36242625.
sourceReferences.note: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension prospective cohort, 490 patients over 9 years (J Neurol 2023): highest OCT retinal nerve fibre layer (most severe papilledema) had the worst visual outcomes; delayed visual field and ganglion cell layer decline after 12 months; disease duration and BMI change the key visual prognostic factors; supports the bounded severity-gradient association only.
